title: Graceful Degrade Orbit & Tenant Harbor — PRD sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a unified approach to handling overload and capacity scarcity in Dedicated pools. 'Orbit' describes graceful-degrade tiers for live traffic. 'Harbor' describes tenant-facing lanes and admission controls that let customers trade off fidelity vs latency/cost during contention.

Motivation
- Customers want predictable behavior when capacity is constrained (avoid hard failures, avoid silent latencies spikes).
- Existing burst/soft-reserve designs are piecemeal; operational burden remains high.
- We need an interpret-able, testable orchestration that can be exposed as opt-in product controls.

Goals
- Provide deterministic, observable degrade paths with minimal customer config.
- Maintain strong isolation guarantees: noisey tenants should not collapse others.
- Allow controlled, billable burst with clear SLAs and rollback semantics.
- Surface easy knobs in Console and an API for advanced customers.

Core concepts (short)
1) Orbit tiers (runtime):
   - Orbit-0 (full fidelity): normal execution with full KV cache and batching.
   - Orbit-1 (latency-first degrade): reduce batching window, enable prefix caching, mild quantization profile.
   - Orbit-2 (economy/approx): aggressive quantize, drop non-essential tokens (tooling hooks), best-effort fallback model variant.
   - Orbit-Safe (isolation fallback): for tenants hit by noisy neighbors — spin up sandboxed execution lanes with limited throughput, explicit error surface.

2) Tenant Harbor (admission + billing lanes):
   - Harbor-Reserve: tenant has reserved slots (committed capacity). Always stays in Orbit-0 unless pool-level emergency.
   - Harbor-Opportunistic: can borrow headroom at higher rate; uses burst-currency accounting and can be evicted to Harbor-Safe.
   - Harbor-Elastic: default self-serve; subject to predictive autoscaler decisions and transient degrade.

3) Delta-Burst tokens
   - Tokens represent short-lived headroom. Issued from global pool when spare capacity exists. Tokens are charged immediately to tenant ledger and expire. Eviction rules use token age and tenant priority.

Autoscaler & admission model (outline)
- Predictive autoscaler keeps a per-pool short-horizon forecast (30s–10m) driven by request-rate + model-seq-length distribution.
- Admission controller consults: pool occupancy, token ledger, tenant priority, recent P99s and cache-hit-rates.
- Admission results: admit-normal (Orbit-0), admit-degraded (Orbit-1/2), queue, or reject-with-suggestion.

Isolation controls
- Soft-siloing: allocate per-tenant concurrency floor and a borrowable ceiling. Floors are enforced via admission; ceilings via weighted fair-share.
- Noisy-tenant detectors: high variance in KV miss + sudden spikes triggers immediate micro-sandbox (Orbit-Safe) and operator alert.
- Tenant-level QoS profiles: customers can opt into conservative mode (strict floors) or elastic mode (more burst risk).

Degradation choreography (how we move between orbits)
- Primary signals: P99 latency > target, queue depth > threshold, GPU utilization > 95%, KV cache hit drop > 15pp.
- Transition rules: prefer downgrade to Orbit-1 first; if metrics worsen, escalate to Orbit-2.
- Recovery: hold for stabilization window (configurable; default 60s) and ramp back to higher orbit gradually.
- Safety: persistent degradations longer than X minutes trigger on-call runbook.

Operational runbook (ops-friendly)
- Play 1 (auto-heal): autoscaler opens prewarm ephemeral slots; token issuer pauses for pool while prewarm completes.
- Play 2 (tenant quarantine): move offending tenant to Harbor-Safe, notify tenant, surface mitigation options in Console.
- Play 3 (eviction): if global emergency, follow eviction microcontract: oldest opportunistic tokens first, then elastic tenants by decayed priority.

API & Console surfaces (product notes)
- New fields in capacity config: orbit_policy (conservative|balanced|aggressive), harbor_mode (reserve|opportunistic|elastic), burst_budget (tokens/min).
- Console: pool heatmap showing orbit transitions, per-tenant token ledger, and 'Simulate degrade' button for testing.

Telemetry & SLOs to capture
- Token issuance rate, token burnback, and expiration rate.
- Orbit transition counts and dwell times per pool and tenant.
- KV cache hit rate, batch size distribution, P50/P95/P99 latencies per orbit.
- Chargeback delta per tenant (how much burst cost they incurred).

Simulation & validation plan (short)
- Extend existing dedicated-sim to support orbit transitions and token ledger (see linked PR).
- Scenarios: sudden 10x traffic, slow ramp over 30m, noisy-tenant spike, multi-pool coupling.
- Success criteria: P99s for reserved tenants should not regress > 10% under all but catastrophic scenarios; eviction fairness score within 2% of target.

Open questions / trade-offs
- Billing semantics: immediate charge on token issuance vs amortized charge across completed requests. (ops prefers immediate for accounting).
- How visible should Orbit changes be to end users of the API? Full transparency could allow gameable behavior.
- Complexity vs explainability: can we provide simple presets that cover 90% of cases?

Next steps (short-term)
- Tech spike: prototype token ledger + admission plugin (Ethan + Diego) — 3w.
- Simulation run and measurement: produce metrics for 4 canonical scenarios — 2w.
- Console mockups for token ledger and pool heatmap (Priya) — 1w.
- Cross-team sync with SRE to validate operator runbooks and alert thresholds — 1wk.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a high-level sketch; I want feedback on the eviction microcontract semantics and on the UI metaphors.
- If we like the Orbit/Harbor vocabulary we should standardize naming in telemetry and docs.

Slack threads and refs
- #eng-dedicated: thread 'orbit-proposal' (link in Confluence doc)
- Related work: predictive-autoscaler (confluence), burst-currency ledger (design notes), dedicated-sim PR linked above.
